header.running_head: 3. The Rights and Duties of Muslims

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو ﵄ قَالَ: قِيْلَ لِرَسُوْلِ اللهِ ﷺ: اَيُّ النَّاسِ اَفْضَلُ؟ قَالَ: كُلُّ مَخْمُوْمِ الْقَلْبِ صَدُوْقِ اللِّسَانِ، قَالُوْا: صَدُوْقُ اللِّسَانِ نَعْرِفُهُ فَمَا مَخْمُوْمُ الْقَلْبِ؟ قَالَ: هُوَ التَّقِيُّ النَّقِيُّ لَا اِثْمَ فِيْهِ وَلَا بَغْيَ وَلَا غِلَّ وَلَا حَسَدَ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه ابن ماجه باب الورع والتقوي رقم:٤٢١٦
blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Abdullah ibn Amr (RA) narrates that the Prophet ﷺ was asked, “Who is the best of people?” Rasulullah ﷺ said, “Those who have a makhmum heart and a tongue that speaks the truth.” When the Sahabah (RA) asked, “We know the one with a tongue that speaks the truth. What is the meaning of a makhmum heart?” the Prophet ﷺ said, “The makhmum is one who is God-fearing and pure, who carries no burden of sin or injustice upon himself, and whose heart has no deceit or envy towards others.”

blocks.text:
Explanation:- One with a pure heart means one who is pure from thoughts of anything other than Allah Ta'ala, from wrong thoughts and from wrong intentions.
(Mazahir-e-Haq)

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ مَسْعُوْدٍ ﵁ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُوْل اللهِ ﷺ: لَا يُبَلِّغْنِيْ اَحَدٌ مِنْ اَصْحاَبِيْ عَنْ اَحَدٍ شَيْئًا فَاِنّيْ اُحِبُّ اَنْ اَخْرُجَ اِلَيْكُمْ
